headline: DrivingBench reports one successful low-speed physical-car course completion by GPT-6 Astra in a four-model evaluation
summary: A preprint and its authors’ benchmark site describe a closed-course test in which four general-purpose vision-language models controlled steering and speed in a 2022 Toyota Corolla through a 127 m cone course, using vendor-native agent harnesses and up to three attempts in one conversation. The authors report GPT-6 Astra was the only model to finish, on attempt 2; Claude Fable 5.1 reached 45% on attempt 3, while no other attempt passed 50%. The test used a human operator ready to brake, a single course and one evaluation session per model. The arXiv paper reports Astra’s finish at 4:44 after its first command, while the live site and attempt trace list 5:22; the timing difference is unresolved. This is evidence of a narrow author-reported physical-control result, not general road-driving ability or vehicle safety.
